correctness.rationale: For any finite or countably infinite index set and absolutely summable real signed coefficients, center–leaf distances show the exact Lipschitz seminorm, and zero total mass permits translating potentials to minimum supremum norm. Two normalized one-sided extrema reduce the support problem to the edges of a square; both fractional edge derivatives have constant sign, leaving three corner values. The explicit centered sign potential and two one-sided potentials each meet the corresponding value and BL unit norm. The all-zero, one-sign, infinite-index, equality-boundary and arbitrary positive arm-radius cases were checked. A separate finite LP confirmed 1,500 random cases; no inference about infinity depends on sampling.

originality.rationale: The specific norm identity and sharp radius-dependent mass-ratio phase law for all finite and countably infinite equiradial stars were not present in the materially inspected 2022 and 2023 primary full texts. The 2022 general finite-metric linear program supplies a computational route but does not give the evaluated symbolic identity or countable-star formula; the 2023 general extreme-point theorem supplies norming function existence rather than this classification. Published mathematical search results closest to the topic concern Lipschitz-free octahedrality and numerical indices, distinct invariants. The 2012 empirical-measure algorithm remains an acknowledged full-text uncertainty and unindexed equivalent formulas are possible; no absolute priority or independent certification is claimed.
residual_risks: The older 2012 empirical-measure computational primary full text was not accessible, so an uninspected specialized result cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: Bounded-Lipschitz dual distance between signed atomic measures is a natural functional-analytic measure invariant, and equal-arm stars are canonical tree metrics. For all dimensions, radii and absolutely summable countable data, the exact norm depends on only the leaf total variation and net signed mass rather than a growing-dimensional optimization. It yields a sharp radius-sensitive optimizer-switch boundary and includes the infinite countable case. The natural complete norm classification is useful for benchmark computations and comparing discrete measures; no general theorem for arbitrary trees is claimed.
